_meta.indication: LIVALO is a HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor indicated for patients with primary hyperlipidemia and mixed dyslipidemia as an adjunctive therapy to diet to reduce elevated total cholesterol (TC), LDL-C, apolipoprotein B (Apo B), triglycerides (TG), and to increase HDL-C.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, multicenter, double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled, non-inferiority study; 12-week treatment with either LIVALO or atorvastatin after a 6- to 8-week wash-out/dietary lead-in period.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with primary hyperlipidemia or mixed dyslipidemia.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Percent reduction in LDL-C from baseline to the end of 12 weeks of treatment; non-inferiority demonstrated if lower bound of the 95% CI for the mean treatment difference was greater than -6%.
pivotal_trials.result: LIVALO was non-inferior to atorvastatin for both pairwise comparisons (LIVALO 2 mg vs atorvastatin 10 mg and LIVALO 4 mg vs atorvastatin 20 mg); mean treatment differences (95% CI) were 0% (-3%, 3%) and 1% (-2%, 4%). Mean % LDL-C change from baseline at Week 12: LIVALO 2 mg -38%, LIVALO 4 mg -45%.

nct_ctgov.title: Study to Compare the Efficacy of Pitavastatin With That of Atorvastatin in Lowering Cholesterol Levels

key_safety: The most frequent adverse reactions (rate >=2.0% in at least one marketed dose) were myalgia, back pain, diarrhea, constipation and pain in extremity. Myopathy and rhabdomyolysis with acute renal failure have been reported and increase in a dose-dependent manner.
target_moa: Pitavastatin competitively inhibits HMG-CoA reductase, the rate-determining enzyme in cholesterol biosynthesis, inhibiting cholesterol synthesis in the liver; this upregulates LDL-receptors, accelerates LDL uptake, and decreases plasma total cholesterol.
modality: Small molecule (synthetic lipid-lowering agent for oral administration)

advisory_committee.vote: NDA 22-363 was not referred to an advisory committee for review; because pitavastatin is the eighth statin approved and no new significant efficacy or safety issues were identified, an advisory committee meeting was not considered necessary.

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for addition of safety data to the Livalo package insert based on the study NK-104-4.05US (NCT 01301066), entitled, *A 12-Week, Randomized, Double-Blind, Active-Controlled, Parallel-Group Study Comparing Pitavastatin 4 mg vs. Pravastatin 40 mg in HIV-Infected Subjects with Dyslipidemia*, followed by *a 40-Week Safety Extension Study*.

description.text: Added pediatric patients 8 years and older with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH)

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for revisions in the United States Package Insert (USPI) for Livalo to incorporate safety and efficacy data of pitavastatin use in pediatric patients 8 years and older with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH) to reduce elevated TC, LDL-C, and Apo B to fulfill the requirements of a Written Request issued by FDA to Kowa Pharmaceuticals America, Inc. on November 2, 2016.

summary.text: Standard NDA under section 505(b) of the FDCA for pitavastatin (the eighth statin approved); approved first cycle with no accelerated approval or special designations, not referred to an advisory committee, with two postmarketing requirements (severe renal impairment PK trial and a lopinavir/ritonavir drug-drug interaction trial).

citations.quote: Please refer to the new drug application (NDA) you submitted on behalf of Kowa Company, Limited, dated October 1, 2008, received October 3, 2008, submitted under section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) for Livalo® (pitavastatin) Tablets, 1 mg, 2 mg, and 4 mg.

NDA 22-363 was not referred to an advisory committee for review. Because pitavastatin is the eighth statin approved and there were no new significant efficacy or safety issues identified during the review of the application, other than those already identified for the statin drug class, an advisory committee meeting was not considered necessary.
